PE1-27.hint: The sign of \(a\) gives the direction. The vertex has \(x = -\dfrac{b}{2a}\); substitute that into \(q\) to get the \(y\)-value. The range starts (or ends) at the \(y\)-value of the vertex.
slips: Writing the axis of symmetry as \(y = 2\). It is a vertical line, \(x = 2\).
Dropping the negative sign in \(-\dfrac{b}{2a}\) and getting \(x = -2\).
Writing the range as \([2,\infty)\). The range uses the \(y\)-value of the vertex, \(-5\).

PE1-28.hint: Factor the leading coefficient out of the \(x^{2}\) and \(x\) terms. Inside the parentheses add and subtract the square of half the middle coefficient.
slips: Adding \(4\) inside the parentheses without subtracting it. The \(3\) multiplies it, so you have changed the function by \(12\).
Using \(\left(\dfrac{12}{2}\right)^{2} = 36\) without first factoring out the \(3\).
